items.content_excerpt: $ONDS Could Anduril Be a Catalyst? Anduril’s reported $90B valuation is putting autonomous defense tech in a whole new spotlight. With a potential IPO still ahead, investors may start reassessing the entire sector. Remember the SpaceX effect? IPO rumors and soaring private valuations helped draw attention to publicly traded space stocks. Could Anduril do something similar for defense tech? Ondas is building across autonomous drones, counter-UAS and robotics. If ONDS eventually reaches $2.2B in annual revenue in 27-28, what could it be worth? Anduril is being valued at 40x sales, Give Ondas roughly half that 15–20x sales, that’s a $33B–$44B valuation. Using a $3.45B starting market cap and constant shares, that would imply roughly $58–$77SHARE from a $6.04 reference price. Highly speculative, not a price target. Revenue execution, profitability and dilution matter. Will the market value Ondas on today’s numbers or tomorrow’s autonomous defense opportunity? I can’t fkn wait

items.title: Tech got wrecked this week! Nasdaq fell 2.1% today & 4.5% for the week, its worst week since late June! $QQQ dropped about 2.5% today &a
items.content_excerpt: Tech got wrecked this week! Nasdaq fell 2.1% today & 4.5% for the week, its worst week since late June! $QQQ dropped about 2.5% today & about 5.5% for the week! What's driving the tech drop? AI debt fears: chip stocks slid for 9 straight sessions, & $CRWV fell almost 12% today on worries about how AI data centers are being financed. Hot inflation: September CPI came in above expectations & PPI’s reports didn’t help either, so rates will likely stay higher for longer. The 10-year yield is near 5.08%. Rotation: money moved out of tech into energy, materials & banks. The Dow actually gained 1.5% this week! Megacaps felt pain too: $META fell about 3.7% today, & $NVDA & $SMH got caught in the chip drop. Context matters because the Nasdaq hit an all-time high just 10 days ago, & $QQQ remains up ~14.5% YTD despite trading roughly 7% below its peak. Pullbacks of 5–10% are normal after big runs. Opportunity or a warning sign?

Cars are becoming robots. Soon, millions of vehicles, robots and AI systems could communicate, exchange information and even make transactions autonomously. But which networks will power this future? As machines become more autonomous, the networks they rely on could become just as important as the technology itself.

items.title: Microsoft is expanding its custom Maia AI chip business to lower the cost of running artificial intelligence workloads and improve returns o
items.content_excerpt: Microsoft is expanding its custom Maia AI chip business to lower the cost of running artificial intelligence workloads and improve returns on its massive infrastructure investments. Developing its own chips could help the company reduce reliance on external suppliers such as Nvidia, gain greater control over computing capacity and make AI services more cost-efficient as demand continues to grow. However, lower computing costs do not automatically translate into higher profits. Investors must determine how much of the savings Microsoft can retain and how much it may pass on to customers through lower prices for AI tools and cloud services. Greater efficiency could boost margins if the company maintains pricing, but intensifying competition could force Microsoft to share those savings with customers. The financial impact will also depend on the performance and scalability of Maia chips, development expenses and the enormous capital required to build and operate AI data centers $MSFT $NVDA

items.title: Tech got wrecked this week! Nasdaq fell 2.1% today & 4.5% for the week, its worst week since late June! $QQQ dropped about 2.5% today &a
items.content_excerpt: Tech got wrecked this week! Nasdaq fell 2.1% today & 4.5% for the week, its worst week since late June! $QQQ dropped about 2.5% today & about 5.5% for the week! What's driving the tech drop? AI debt fears: chip stocks slid for 9 straight sessions, & $CRWV fell almost 12% today on worries about how AI data centers are being financed. Hot inflation: September CPI came in above expectations & PPI’s reports didn’t help either, so rates will likely stay higher for longer. The 10-year yield is near 5.08%. Rotation: money moved out of tech into energy, materials & banks. The Dow actually gained 1.5% this week! Megacaps felt pain too: $META fell about 3.7% today, & $NVDA & $SMH got caught in the chip drop. Context matters because the Nasdaq hit an all-time high just 10 days ago, & $QQQ remains up ~14.5% YTD despite trading roughly 7% below its peak. Pullbacks of 5–10% are normal after big runs. Opportunity or a warning sign?

items.content_excerpt: $TSM $SPCX $PLTR $NVDA Monday, October 19, 1987—known as Black Monday—was the worst single-day percentage decline in the history of the Dow Jones Industrial Average. The Dow fell 22.61%, losing 508 points in one trading session. And there is a striking calendar coincidence: October 19, 2026, is also a Monday, exactly 39 years later. The important lesson from 1987 is not the anniversary. It is how a combination of high valuations, changing interest-rate expectations, selling pressure and automated trading strategies created a self-reinforcing decline.

items.title: Emergent BioSolutions announced that CFO Richard Lindahl will retire at the end of 2026 after serving in the role since 2018. Frank Vargo, t
items.content_excerpt: Emergent BioSolutions announced that CFO Richard Lindahl will retire at the end of 2026 after serving in the role since 2018. Frank Vargo, the company’s vice president and treasurer, will become interim CFO on January 1, 2027, with Lindahl remaining as a senior executive adviser from January through March to support the transition. Lindahl previously held senior finance and CFO positions at CEB and Sprint Nextel and currently serves on the board of Compass Therapeutics. Vargo, 43, joined Emergent in December 2019 in corporate financial planning and analysis, became vice president and treasurer in November 2025, and previously held finance roles at Under Armour and in the aerospace and defense sector. CEO Joe Papa said Vargo has been instrumental in advancing the company’s strategic priorities. The transition comes as Emergent continues a multiyear transformation plan focused on strengthening its business and improving operational performance. $EBS

items.content_excerpt: $STZ The post-earnings verdict on Constellation is a split screen. items.content_excerpt: Hut 8 shares fell after on-chain analytics firms reported that wallets linked to the company transferred approximately 1,966 BTC, worth around $161M, to cryptocurrency exchanges and over-the-counter trading desks over seven days, emptying a position previously held in Coinbase Prime. The transfers raised concerns that Hut 8 may be liquidating a significant portion of its Bitcoin treasury, despite management’s earlier indication that Bitcoin exposure would increasingly reside within its subsidiary American Bitcoin. Additional pressure came from Cantor Fitzgerald’s October 12 price-target cut to $151 from $180, bearish put-option activity and insider transactions. The CFO reduced his holdings by approximately 26% in a transaction attributed to tax-withholding obligations on vested shares, amid roughly $2.5B in reported insider sales over the past three months. Hut 8’s Q3 2026 results are scheduled for November 4, leaving investors with limited near-term fundamental catalysts. $HUT $BTC.X

items.title: $MLTX I'd like to add: Substantiation of results across independent, adequate and well-controlled trials can help provide strong evidenc
items.content_excerpt: $MLTX I'd like to add: Substantiation of results across independent, adequate and well-controlled trials can help provide strong evidence of effectiveness. Multiple adequate and well-controlled trials within a development program can have identical or different designs. Although positive results from two identically designed trials can provide substantial evidence of effectiveness, the conclusions from precisely replicated trials (or from a single trial) may be vulnerable to any systematic biases or limitations inherent to the particular trial design and conduct. In contrast, positive results from two nonidentical trials may be more persuasive, as unrecognized flaws may be less likely to impact the outcomes of both trials. Furthermore, two nonidentical trials can provide additional information about a drug’s effect. MIRA 234 patients (providing SEE) VELA-1 283 patients (SEE, 2nd trial) VELA-2 276 patients (adding data to reinforce safety profile) VELA-TEEN: first adequate trial ever.
